title: She kept it hidden.
paragraphs: Because not everything God does in you is meant for public explanation.
Some things… are too holy to post too early.
And if you don’t understand this, you will expose what heaven told you to treasure.
She didn’t try to impress people with divine encounters.
And that’s where most of us fail.
We perform spirituality instead of protecting intimacy.
And slowly, quietly… we lose the weight of what God is doing in us.
Some of you are not confused because God is silent.
You are confused because you have not learned how to sit with what He already said.
Explained it before it was ready.
This is the war inside the soul.
But God gives you a seed.
But God gives you a whisper.
But God gives you a mystery.
And what you do next will determine whether your faith deepens…
Let’s talk about the part we avoid.
Because sometimes, we don’t share because we’re led by God.
We share because we’re driven by ego.
Because if no one sees it, we start questioning if it even matters.
We want to look anointed instead of being formed.
We want to sound deep instead of going deep.
We want people to affirm what God is still developing.
And when the applause comes too early…
the roots never grow deep enough to sustain the weight of the calling.
Mary teaches us something violent to our pride.
She teaches us how to be hidden without being insecure.
She teaches us how to carry something divine without needing to display it.
She teaches us how to trust God in silence.
“But Mary treasured up all these things, pondering them in her heart.”
To treasure means to guard, to preserve, to hold with intention.
To let it sink below surface-level understanding.
Some scholars interpret this as Mary actively processing divine revelation over time—not instant comprehension, but faithful reflection.
Can you carry something you don’t fully understand…
Because here is the deeper issue.
This is not just about patience.
This is about the condition of your heart.
What you do with what God reveals…
Will you let it shape you?
Or will you use it to shape how people see you?
This is where we confront the truth.
Not everyone who talks about God is walking with God.
Not everyone who posts revelation is living in obedience.
Not everyone who sounds spiritual is surrendered.
We can speak in ways that sound deep.
There’s a need to be seen.
And that is where the Gospel confronts us.
Because the real issue is not just behavior.
Sin is not just what we do.
And no amount of “better habits” can fix a sinful heart.
And this is where everything turns.
Mary did not just treasure moments.
The One she held in mystery…
would one day hang in clarity.
Because here’s the truth we cannot escape.
We have all chosen ourselves over God.
But God did not leave us there.
Jesus lived the life we could not live.
Then He went to the cross.
He took the punishment we deserved.
And when He said, “It is finished,”
He meant the debt was paid in full.
Over everything that once held you captive.
Through repentance and faith in Jesus Christ alone.
You can come to Him as you are.
And He will not reject you.
He will teach you how to treasure again.
So let me ask you directly.
What have you exposed too early?
What have you treated casually that God called sacred?
What have you used for image that was meant for transformation?
Back to a heart that listens.
Back to a faith that doesn’t rush.
You don’t have to keep living shallow.
You don’t have to keep chasing validation.
You don’t have to keep performing.
And if this is your prayer—

“Jesus… I’m done performing.
I’m done pretending.
Change my heart.
Teach me to treasure You.”
If this stirred something in you…
